title: Release cadence experiments — personal scratchpad
content:
Goal: iterate on release cadence and safety guardrails to reduce customer-facing regressions while keeping time-to-ship < 48h for high-priority fixes.

Background/why:
- We currently do weekly deploys to hosted and ad-hoc for dedicated/private. Several regressions over last 3 months correlated with denser release cadence + model changes.
- Hypothesis: slightly longer, instrumented windows + staggered customer cohorts reduces undetected regressions while not blocking engineers.

Hypotheses to test (ranked):
1) Introducing a 6-hour micro-window (10% traffic) for fast rollouts catches infra/latency regressions earlier than 100% progressive rollout.
2) A two-stage canary (10% static cohort, then 10% random ramp) identifies client-protocol regressions (edge cases) more reliably.
3) Pinning inference model minor versions for 72h after deploy reduces immediate-quality regressions but increases ops churn — tradeoff measurable.

Experiment design sketch:
- Variant A (short fast): deploy -> 10% micro-window (6h) -> if green, 50% for 2h -> full.
- Variant B (two-stage): deploy -> 10% static cohort for 12h (cohort of enterprise pilot customers) -> 10% randomized ramp (6h) -> 100%.
- Variant C (pin): deploy -> 100% but force client-side model pin for 72h for new model revision; observe quality regressions vs baseline.

Primary metrics (SLOs + safety):
- 95th/99th latency pre/post (serving runtime) — alert if > +30% over baseline.
- Error rate (HTTP 5xx + runtime exceptions) — alert if +3x baseline or absolute >0.5% over 15m.
- Quality regressions: eval-set BLEU/ROUGE-like delta (or LM-quality delta on golden prompts) — alert if > pre-defined delta by model.
- Customer-facing incidents (pager count) and rollback events.
- Time-to-detect (median) for any regression in experiment groups.

Gates and rollback heuristics (quick):
- Automatic rollback triggers: 5xx rate surpasses 0.5% sustained for 10m OR 95p latency +100ms sustained 15m.
- Manual gates: if golden-eval loss increases by threshold or key customer reports >2 degraded sessions.
- Soft-fallback: route failing requests to previous model variant when latency spikes (circuit-breaker).

Observability checklist (what to instrument before running):
- Per-cohort latency and error dashboards (10% micro-window view).
- Golden-set automated eval run every 20m against production canaries; post-deploy diffs surfaced in rollout UI.
- Telemetry tagging: release_id, cohort_id, client_tier, model_minor_version.
- Short-lived trace sampling for canary cohort (higher sampling rate).

Operational playbook (scratchy):
- Preflight: confirm rollout job uses release_id tag + cohort mapping.
- Kickoff: announce in #releases, include baseline metrics snapshot and expected rollback thresholds.
- During micro-window: SRE watches latency/errors + golden-eval dashboard. If anomaly -> pause ramp + hotfix or rollback.
- Post-success: mark release as "observed" for 72h and do daily quick-eval.

Edge cases / open questions:
- How to define static cohort (variant B)? list of customers? opt-in header? we could create an API key flag for pilot customers.
- Client pin: forcing pin for 72h requires client SDK change or route-level header detection. Ops overhead?
- Interaction with Dedicated customers — they may be on different cadence. Need mapping before test.

Quick commands & stories:
- Deploy command (local): ./deploy --release-id=R1234 --cohort=10pct-micro --model=minorprefix-2025-01
- Hotfix rollback (manual): infra-cli rollback --release R1234 --to-release R1229 --reason="latency-spike"

Risks and mitigation notes: 
- Risk: oscillation when multiple teams adopt micro-windows. Mitigation: central release calendar and per-team minimum spacing (24h).
- Risk: golden-set blind spots. Mitigation: expand golden set to include low-resource prompts and long-context cases.

Mini-checklist before flipping experiment on:
- [ ] Dashboard per-cohort created + shared in channel
- [ ] Golden-set run wired to alerting (critical)
- [ ] Cohort mapping file uploaded (if using static cohort)
- [ ] Ops runbook updated with rollback commands
- [ ] Stakeholders notified (SRE, product, solutions eng)

Notes to self / follow-ups:
- Talk to Solutions Eng about pilot customers willing to be static cohort (Samir?).
- Ask SDK team if we can bake an opt-in header for model pinning by next sprint.
- Add a lightweight load test for micro-window cadence to validate burst autoscale behavior.

Potential success criteria (end of experiment):
- 30% reduction in mean-time-to-detect regressions for release-related incidents vs baseline
- No statistically significant increase in customer-facing incidents during ramp windows
- Engineering-deploy time (time from PR merge -> canary) remains <=48h for high-priority fixes

Housekeeping: store experiment artifacts under (temp): /shared_drives/engineering/release-experiments/213_cadence_experiment/
(once we are past smoke, move final runbooks to Confluence)

Bottom line: start small (Variant A) in staging and one pilot account, iterate telemetry first. Keep everything reversible and clearly visible.

End of scratchpad.
